title: Hydropower Licensing Transparency Act
official_title: To amend the Federal Power Act to require the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to annually submit to Congress a report on the status of ongoing hydropower relicensing applications.
likelihoodReason: Introduced by Rep. Schrier (D-WA) with Rep. Fulcher (R-ID) and 3 cosponsors; passed the House and was ordered reported favorably by the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee. A bipartisan reporting-transparency measure with no spending or regulatory mandate tends to clear the Senate when floor time allows.
summary: Requires federal energy regulators to send Congress an annual report on the status of hydropower dam relicensing applications that have been pending for years.
brief: Requires FERC to submit an annual report to Congress on the status of long-pending hydropower relicensing applications.

top_lines.headline: Hydropower Relicensing Reports
subs: FERC must report annually on pending relicensing applications
Covers licenses where notice was given 3+ years earlier
First report due within 180 days of enactment

items.main: Names the Act the “Hydropower Relicensing Transparency Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Requires FERC to report to Congress every year on hydropower relicensing applications that remain pending after early notice.
items.detail: Adds subsection (g) to Section 15 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. 808). Within 180 days of enactment and annually after, FERC must report on each new license where the existing licensee notified the Commission (under subsection (b)(1)) at least 3 years before the report that it intended to apply, but the new license has not yet been issued. Each report must include the notice date, any docket number, whether an application was filed, the status and anticipated issue date, upcoming proceedings, and any required actions by the licensee, FERC, and fish and wildlife agencies.

gaps: The bill requires annual status reports on delayed relicensing but sets no deadline for FERC to actually issue the licenses.
It requires reporting on applications pending 3+ years after notice but does not address applications where notice was given more recently.

featured_quotes.name: Ms. Schrier
featured_quotes.text: I am from Washington State, and in the Pacific Northwest, hydropower makes up the majority of our energy mix. That is why I am very proud to lead this effort to enhance transparency and really help streamline the non-Federal hydropower licensing process with my colleague from Idaho, Representative Fulcher.

added: Annual FERC report to Congress on the status of long-pending hydropower relicensing applications (new subsection (g) of Federal Power Act Section 15)
Report now also covers subsequent licenses (where sections 14 and 15 are waived), not just new licenses
Report now covers original licenses under section 4(e) sought by a citizen, association, corporation, State, Indian Tribe, or municipality with 3-years-prior notice
New requirement: report information must be disaggregated by license type — new/subsequent license under section 15 vs. original license under section 4(e)
modified: Short title changed from "Hydropower Relicensing Transparency Act" to "Hydropower Licensing Transparency Act"
Report mechanism restructured from a new subsection 15(g) of the Federal Power Act into a new standalone section 37 (inserted after section 36, 16 U.S.C. 823g)
Report items broadened to also reference subsequent and original licenses and their non-licensee applicants throughout
